[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#92-94)#### pub fn [instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.instr_seq)(&mut self, id: [InstrSeqId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.InstrSeqId.html)) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#92-94)

#### pub fn [instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.instr_seq)(&mut self, id: [InstrSeqId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.InstrSeqId.html)) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

Continue building and mutating an existing instruction sequence.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
let mut block = builder.dangling_instr_seq(None);
let id = block.id();
// Build up the block some.
block
    .f64_const(1337.0)
    .drop();
// Do some other stuff...
drop(block);
// Use `instr_seq` to get the builder for the block again, and build
// some more things onto it.
let mut block = builder.instr_seq(id);
block
    .i32_const(42)
    .drop();
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#130-134)#### pub fn [dangling_instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.dangling_instr_seq)(
    &mut self,
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#130-134)

#### pub fn [dangling_instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.dangling_instr_seq)(
    &mut self,
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

Create a new instruction sequence that is unreachable.

It is your responsibility to

-
make a `Instr::Block`,`Instr::Loop`, or`Instr::IfElse`that uses this instruction sequence, and
-
append that `Instr`into a parent instruction sequence via`InstrSeqBuilder::instr`or`InstrSeqBuilder::instr_at`

or else this built up instruction sequence will never be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use walrus::ir::*;
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
// Create an empty, dangling instruction sequemce.
let mut seq = builder.dangling_instr_seq(None);
let seq_id = seq.id();
// Do stuff with the sequence...
drop(seq);
// Finally, make our instruction sequence reachable by adding an
// block/loop/if-else instruction that uses it to a reachable instruction
// sequence.
builder
    .func_body()
    .instr(Block { seq: seq_id });
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#153-156)#### pub fn [finish](https://docs.rs#method.finish)(
    self,
    args: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[LocalId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.LocalId.html)>,
    funcs: &mut [ModuleFunctions](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleFunctions.html),
) -> [FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#153-156)

#### pub fn [finish](https://docs.rs#method.finish)(
    self,
    args: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[LocalId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.LocalId.html)>,
    funcs: &mut [ModuleFunctions](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleFunctions.html),
) -> [FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html)

Finishes this builder, wrapping it all up and inserting it into the
specified `Module`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
builder
    .func_body()
    .i32_const(1234)
    .drop();
let function_id = builder.finish(vec![], &mut module.funcs);
```

# IdsToIndices in walrus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/walrus/^0.23/struct.IdsToIndices.html

`pub struct IdsToIndices { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Maps our high-level identifiers to the raw indices they end up emitted at.

As we lower to raw wasm structures, we cement various constructs’ locations
in their respective index spaces. For example, a type with some id `A` ends
up being the `i^th` type emitted in the raw wasm type section. When a
function references that type, it needs to reference it by its `i` index
since the identifier `A` doesn’t exist at the raw wasm level.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# IndicesToIds in walrus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/walrus/^0.23/struct.IndicesToIds.html

`pub struct IndicesToIds { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Maps from old indices in the original Wasm binary to `walrus` IDs.

This is intended to be used with `walrus::Module`s that were parsed from
some existing Wasm binary. `walrus::Module`s that are built up from scratch,
and not originally parsed from an existing Wasm binary, will have an empty
`IndicesToIds`.

For example, this allows you to get the `walrus::FunctionId` of some Wasm
function when you have its old index in the original Wasm module.

Any newly built or added things (functions, tables, types, etc) are not associated with an old index (since they were not present in the original Wasm binary).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

# InstrSeqBuilder in walrus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/walrus/^0.23/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html

`pub struct InstrSeqBuilder<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A builder returned by instruction sequence-construction methods to build up instructions within a block/loop/if-else over time.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Append a new, nested `block ... end` to this builder’s sequence.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example:

```
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
// Append the following WAT to the function:
//
//     block
//       i32.const 1337
//       drop
//     end
builder
    .func_body()
    .block(None, |block| {
        block
            .i32_const(1337)
            .drop();
    });
```

Append a new, nested `block ... end` to this builder’s sequence.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example:

```
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
// Make the function's body be a single `unreachable` instruction.
builder
    .func_body()
    .unreachable();
// Splice the following WAT into the function, before the `unreachable`:
//
//     block
//       i32.const 1337
//       drop
//     end
builder
    .func_body()
    .block_at(0, None, |block| {
        block
            .i32_const(1337)
            .drop();
    });
```

    &mut self,
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
    consequent: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
    alternative: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#410-434)

#### pub fn [if_else](https://docs.rs#method.if_else)(
    &mut self,
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
    consequent: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
    alternative: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
) -> &mut Self

Build a new `if <consequent> else <alternative> end` instruction
sequence.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

```
use walrus::ValType;
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let ty = module.types.add(&[], &[ValType::I32]);
let (flip_coin, _) = module.add_import_func("flip", "coin", ty);
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
builder
    .func_body()
    // (if (call $flip_coin)
    //   (then (i32.const 12))
    //   (else (i32.const 34)))
    .call(flip_coin)
    .if_else(
        ValType::I32,
        |then| {
            then.i32_const(12);
        },
        |else_| {
            else_.i32_const(34);
        },
    );
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#470-498)#### pub fn [if_else_at](https://docs.rs#method.if_else_at)(
    &mut self,
    position: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
    consequent: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
    alternative: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#470-498)

#### pub fn [if_else_at](https://docs.rs#method.if_else_at)(
    &mut self,
    position: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
    consequent: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
    alternative: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>),
) -> &mut Self

Splice a new `if <consequent> else <alternative> end` into this
instruction sequence at the given position.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
use walrus::ValType;
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let ty = module.types.add(&[], &[ValType::I32]);
let (flip_coin, _) = module.add_import_func("flip", "coin", ty);
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
builder
    .func_body()
    .call(flip_coin)
    .unreachable();
// Splice an if/else after the `call` and before the `unreachable`.
builder
    .func_body()
    .if_else_at(
        1,
        ValType::I32,
        |then| {
            then.i32_const(12);
        },
        |else_| {
            else_.i32_const(34);
        },
    );
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#62-65)#### pub fn [func_body](https://docs.rs#method.func_body)(&mut self) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

#### pub fn [func_body](https://docs.rs#method.func_body)(&mut self) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

Get a `InstrSeqBuilder` for building and mutating this function’s body.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#92-94)#### pub fn [instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.instr_seq)(&mut self, id: [InstrSeqId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.InstrSeqId.html)) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#92-94)

#### pub fn [instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.instr_seq)(&mut self, id: [InstrSeqId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.InstrSeqId.html)) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

Continue building and mutating an existing instruction sequence.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
let mut block = builder.dangling_instr_seq(None);
let id = block.id();
// Build up the block some.
block
    .f64_const(1337.0)
    .drop();
// Do some other stuff...
drop(block);
// Use `instr_seq` to get the builder for the block again, and build
// some more things onto it.
let mut block = builder.instr_seq(id);
block
    .i32_const(42)
    .drop();
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#130-134)#### pub fn [dangling_instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.dangling_instr_seq)(
    &mut self,
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/function_builder.rs.html#130-134)

#### pub fn [dangling_instr_seq](https://docs.rs#method.dangling_instr_seq)(
    &mut self,
    ty: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[InstrSeqType](https://docs.rs/ir/enum.InstrSeqType.html)>,
) -> [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>

Create a new instruction sequence that is unreachable.

It is your responsibility to

-
make a `Instr::Block`,`Instr::Loop`, or`Instr::IfElse`that uses this instruction sequence, and
-
append that `Instr`into a parent instruction sequence via`InstrSeqBuilder::instr`or`InstrSeqBuilder::instr_at`

or else this built up instruction sequence will never be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-7)Example

```
use walrus::ir::*;
let mut module = walrus::Module::default();
let mut builder = walrus::FunctionBuilder::new(&mut module.types, &[], &[]);
// Create an empty, dangling instruction sequemce.
let mut seq = builder.dangling_instr_seq(None);
let seq_id = seq.id();
// Do stuff with the sequence...
drop(seq);
// Finally, make our instruction sequence reachable by adding an
// block/loop/if-else instruction that uses it to a reachable instruction
// sequence.
builder
    .func_body()
    .instr(Block { seq: seq_id });
```

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

Whether or not this is a “shared” memory

This is part of the threads proposal.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.memory64)

`memory64: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether or not this is a 64-bit memory.

This is part of the memory64 proposal.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.initial)

`initial: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)Initial size of this memory, in wasm pages.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.maximum)

`maximum: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)>Optional maximum size of this memory, in wasm pages.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.page_size_log2)

`page_size_log2: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>The log base 2 of the memory’s custom page size.

Memory pages are, by default, 64KiB large (i.e. 216 or 65536).

The custom-page-sizes proposal allows changing it to other values.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.import)

`import: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ImportId](https://docs.rs/type.ImportId.html)>Whether or not this memory is imported, and if so from where.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.name)

`name: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>The name of this memory, used for debugging purposes in the `name`
custom section.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Generate a [GraphViz Dot](https://graphviz.org/) file for this module,
showing the relationship between various structures in the module and
its instructions.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

First, generate a `.dot` file with this method:

```
let my_module: walrus::Module = get_module_from_somewhere();
my_module.write_graphviz_dot("my_module.dot")?;
```
Second, use the `dot` command-line tool to render an SVG (or PNG,
etc…):

```
dot my_module.dot \       # Provide our generated `.dot`.
    -T svg \              # Generate an SVG image.
    -o my_module.svg      # Write to this output file.
```

#### pub fn [replace_exported_func](https://docs.rs#method.replace_exported_func)(
    &mut self,
    fid: [FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html),
    builder_fn: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)((&mut [InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html)<'_>, &[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[LocalId](https://docs.rs/ir/type.LocalId.html)>)),
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html)>

Replace a single exported function with the result of the provided builder function.

The builder function is provided a mutable reference to an [ InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html) which can be
used to build the function as necessary.

For example, if you wanted to replace an exported function with a no-op,

The arguments passed to the original function will be passed to the new exported function that was built in your closure.

This function returns the function ID of the *new* function,
after it has been inserted into the module as an export.

Replace a single imported function with the result of the provided builder function.

The builder function is provided a mutable reference to an [ InstrSeqBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.InstrSeqBuilder.html) which can be
used to build the function as necessary.

For example, if you wanted to replace an imported function with a no-op,

The arguments passed to the original function will be passed to the new exported function that was built in your closure.

This function returns the function ID of the *new* function, and
removes the existing import that has been replaced (the function will become local).

#### pub fn [generate_dwarf](https://docs.rs#method.generate_dwarf)(&mut self, generate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Sets a flag to whether DWARF debug sections are generated for this module.

By default this flag is `false`. Note that any emitted DWARF is
currently wildly incorrect and buggy, and is also larger than the wasm
itself!

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#105-108)#### pub fn [generate_name_section](https://docs.rs#method.generate_name_section)(&mut self, generate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#105-108)

#### pub fn [generate_name_section](https://docs.rs#method.generate_name_section)(&mut self, generate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Sets a flag to whether the custom “name” section is generated for this module.

The “name” section contains symbol names for the module, functions,
locals, types, memories, tables, data, elements and globals.
When enabled, stack traces will use these names, instead of
`wasm-function[123]`.

By default this flag is `true`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#116-122)#### pub fn [generate_synthetic_names_for_anonymous_items](https://docs.rs#method.generate_synthetic_names_for_anonymous_items)(

    &mut self,

) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Sets a flag to whether synthetic debugging names are generated for anonymous locals/functions/etc when parsing and running passes for this module.

By default this flag is `false`, and it will generate quite a few names
if enabled!

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#133-136)#### pub fn [strict_validate](https://docs.rs#method.strict_validate)(&mut self, strict: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#133-136)

#### pub fn [strict_validate](https://docs.rs#method.strict_validate)(&mut self, strict: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Indicates whether the module, after parsing, performs strict validation of the wasm module to adhere with the current version of the wasm specification.

This can be expensive for some modules and strictly isn’t required to
create a `Module` from a wasm file. This includes checks such as “atomic
instructions require a shared memory”.

By default this flag is `true`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#145-148)#### pub fn [generate_producers_section](https://docs.rs#method.generate_producers_section)(
    &mut self,
    generate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#145-148)

#### pub fn [generate_producers_section](https://docs.rs#method.generate_producers_section)(
    &mut self,
    generate: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Indicates whether the module will have the “producers” custom section
which preserves the original producers and also includes `walrus`.

This is generally used for telemetry in browsers, but for otherwise tiny wasm binaries can add some size to the binary.

By default this flag is `true`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#159-162)#### pub fn [only_stable_features](https://docs.rs#method.only_stable_features)(&mut self, only: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#159-162)

#### pub fn [only_stable_features](https://docs.rs#method.only_stable_features)(&mut self, only: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Indicates whether this module is allowed to use only stable WebAssembly features or not.

This is currently used to disable some validity checks required by the
WebAssembly specification. It’s not religiously adhered to throughout
the codebase, even if set to `true` some unstable features may still be
allowed.

By default this flag is `false`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#210-216)#### pub fn [on_parse](https://docs.rs#method.on_parse)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#210-216)

#### pub fn [on_parse](https://docs.rs#method.on_parse)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Provide a function that is invoked after successfully parsing a module, and gets access to data structures that only exist at parse time, such as the map from indices in the original Wasm to the new walrus IDs.

This is a good place to parse custom sections that reference things by index.

This will never be invoked for modules that are created from scratch, and are not parsed from an existing Wasm binary.

Note that only one `on_parse` function may be registered and subsequent
registrations will override the old ones.

Note that cloning a `ModuleConfig` will result in a config that does not
have an `on_parse` function, even if the original did.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#222-228)#### pub fn [on_instr_loc](https://docs.rs#method.on_instr_loc)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#222-228)

#### pub fn [on_instr_loc](https://docs.rs#method.on_instr_loc)<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Provide a function that is invoked on source location ID step.

Note that cloning a `ModuleConfig` will result in a config that does not
have an `on_instr_loc` function, even if the original did.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/config.rs.html#233-236)#### pub fn [preserve_code_transform](https://docs.rs#method.preserve_code_transform)(&mut self, preserve: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut [ModuleConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleConfig.html)

Sets a flag to whether code transform is preverved during parsing.

By default this flag is `false`.

# ModuleCustomSections in walrus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/walrus/^0.23/struct.ModuleCustomSections.html

`pub struct ModuleCustomSections { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A collection of custom sections inside a Wasm module.

To add parse and emit your own custom section:

-
Define a `MyCustomSection`type to represent your custom section.
-
Implement the `walrus::CustomSection`trait for your`MyCustomSection`type.
-
When working with a `walrus::Module`named`my_module`, use`my_module.customs.take_raw("my_custom_section_name")`to take ownership of the raw custom section if it is present in the Wasm module.
-
Parse that into your own `MyCustomSection`type in whatever way is appropriate.
-
Do whatever kinds of inspection and manipulation of your `MyCustomSection`type you need to do.
-
Use `my_module.customs.add(my_custom_section)`to add the custom section back into the module, so`walrus`can emit the processed/updated version of the custom section.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/functions/mod.rs.html#201-209)#### pub fn [by_name](https://docs.rs#method.by_name)(&self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/functions/mod.rs.html#201-209)

#### pub fn [by_name](https://docs.rs#method.by_name)(&self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html)>

Get a function ID by its name.

The name used is the “name” custom section name and *not* the export
name, if a function happens to be exported.

Note that function names are *not* guaranteed to be unique. This will
return the first function in the module with the given name.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/functions/mod.rs.html#216-218)#### pub fn [delete](https://docs.rs#method.delete)(&mut self, id: [FunctionId](https://docs.rs/type.FunctionId.html))

Removes a function from this module.

It is up to you to ensure that any potential references to the deleted
function are also removed, eg `call` expressions, exports, table
elements, etc.

Get a shared reference to this module’s functions.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/tables.rs.html#77-97)

Returns the actual table associated with an ID

Removes a table from this module.

It is up to you to ensure that any potential references to the deleted

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/tables.rs.html#132-142)#### pub fn [main_function_table](https://docs.rs#method.main_function_table)(&self) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[TableId](https://docs.rs/type.TableId.html)>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/tables.rs.html#132-142)

#### pub fn [main_function_table](https://docs.rs#method.main_function_table)(&self) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[TableId](https://docs.rs/type.TableId.html)>>

Finds a unique function table in a module.

Modules produced by compilers like LLVM typically have one function
table for indirect function calls. This function will look for a single
function table inside this module, and return that if found. If no
function tables are present `None` will be returned

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an error if there are two function tables in this module

It is up to you to ensure that any potential references to the deleted
type are also removed, eg `call_indirect` expressions, function types,

# DataKind in walrus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/walrus/^0.23/enum.DataKind.html

## Expand description

The kind of data segment: passive or active.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Active)

### Active

An active data segment that is automatically initialized at some address in a static memory.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Passive)

### Passive

A passive data segment that must be manually initialized at a dynamic
address via the `memory.init` instruction (perhaps multiple times in
multiple different memories) and then manually freed when it’s no longer
needed via the `data.drop` instruction.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

reserved its id and associated it with its original input wasm module
index). This should only exist within
`ModuleFunctions::add_local_functions`.

Get the data payload for this custom section.

This should *not* include the section header with id=0, the custom
section’s name, or the count of how many bytes are in the
payload. `walrus` will handle these for you.

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/custom.rs.html#39)#### fn [add_gc_roots](https://docs.rs#method.add_gc_roots)(&self, _roots: &mut [Roots](https://docs.rs/passes/struct.Roots.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/custom.rs.html#39)

#### fn [add_gc_roots](https://docs.rs#method.add_gc_roots)(&self, _roots: &mut [Roots](https://docs.rs/passes/struct.Roots.html))

Add any core wasm roots to the provided `roots` argument.

This function will add any referenced core wasm items into the `Roots`
array provided.

The default provided method does nothing.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/custom.rs.html#57-59)#### fn [apply_code_transform](https://docs.rs#method.apply_code_transform)(&mut self, transform: &[CodeTransform](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeTransform.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/walrus/module/custom.rs.html#57-59)

#### fn [apply_code_transform](https://docs.rs#method.apply_code_transform)(&mut self, transform: &[CodeTransform](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeTransform.html))

Apply the given code transformations to this custom section.

If the module was not configured with `preserve_code_transform = true`,
then this method is never called.

This method is called after we have emitted the non-custom Wasm sections, just before a custom section’s data is emitted into the Wasm binary. If this custom section references offsets in the Wasm code, this is a chance to update them so they are valid for the new, transformed Wasm code that is being emitted.

For example, DWARF debug info references Wasm instructions via offsets into the code section, and we can use these transforms to fix those offsets after having transformed various functions and instructions.

The default provided method does nothing.

# CustomSectionId in walrus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/walrus/^0.23/trait.CustomSectionId.html

```
pub trait CustomSectionId {
    type
```
[CustomSection](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.CustomSection): ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html);
}## Expand description

A common trait for custom section identifiers.

Used in the `ModuleCustomSections::get` family of methods to perform type
conversions from `dyn CustomSection` trait objects into the concrete
`Self::CustomSection` type instance.

You shouldn’t implement this yourself. Instead use `TypedCustomSectionId<T>`
or `UntypedCustomSectionId`.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

---
